title: The Figure over the Basket

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The figure goes twice over a body that cannot answer. The bell goes four, four and a gap, and nobody crosses himself; the account stands as read.
epigraph.attribution: A saying at the Cross, on the first Account-day of Ember

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-eighty-nine-to-one-hundred-and-ninety-one-day-old body carried everywhere and told by nobody --- six months and nine days to six months and eleven days, no roof with a word for it. The surgeon's register colours the noticing (the reading as a figure passed twice over a body that cannot answer, the carrying arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost, the private file turned out as instruments on a towel, a cost carried out of the yard held on a place of its own while the month's figure goes over the basket and does not know it, likenesses taken down one at a time before they can stand up and call themselves a rule) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no new hearing, no tenth stopping, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read and no ending

scenes.title: The First Account-day of Ember
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital: Day 189, Ember 10, Tenthday, before first grey under the Vail kiln-house roof and then down the clay road to the Cross. No recap of the close of Chapter 45: the glaze-room hand went up the clay road breathing on Day 188, his pale line is held on a place of its own and the cost was entered nowhere, and the boy does not join that reading to the day's reading. The boy is one hundred and eighty-nine days old and six months and nine days and nobody under any roof says so (T071/T072). The first smell is hot clay under tallow and wet wool with the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner; the first sound is the kiln drawing breath in fours with a gap, not a bell. Under the floor the carried fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and eighty-nine days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb --- three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). The crust lies leathery two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool is frozen and unwiped; his hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down against the fold. Sella gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, says the house where another woman would say I, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with her hand resting a half-beat longer at the setting, tells the carried fire it is the thaw and says The house will keep it (T058/T079). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, untouched, because a morning, a market and a reading are not openings and the one opening was before the kiln on Ember 1. She carries him down to the Cross at the half-pace from every open slate, gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lies and stands half a pace off, giving no reason to the basket. The bell begins to strike.

scenes.title: Four, Four and a Gap
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 189, no new dated heading: midmorning at the Cross into the going of the light and the small hours under the Vail roof. THE CHAPTER'S ONE MEANINGFUL CHANGE is lived here: the first Account-day and market-day of Ember is read over the basket and the district's arithmetic changes for the month and cannot be undone. Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road to the reading block with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, wipes his thumb twice on his apron before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure, reads one in twelve, as the notice says low into the goers-by, says The levy is called. It is not called by me and your house, never I, and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness; the printed figure stands unchallenged and a figure read aloud is still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047/T077). The bell goes four, four and a gap, longer than a church bell, with nobody crossing himself; the heard bell is kept beside the told bell. Hessa Rale carries Berr's narrow slate up the clay road toward Greybank before noon, held edge-on to her forearm with the writing turned to her sleeve, her hand to the slate before her eyes to the crowd, answering the question put and not the one behind it --- I don't read it. I carry it. There's a difference, and the road doesn't care which and Cross to Greybank. Reading goes up before noon. I've got a road to walk --- no figure coming off the slate, a runner and not a reader, joined to none (T080 advanced, not paid). Below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing, slate to his forearm, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, the market sold over him as water goes over a stone (T090). Across the square at the pot board a silent woman with the sweetish green of lead glaze at one corner of her mouth turns a cup a quarter and sets it back exactly where it stood --- the sixth green still a colour joined to no ear, never Fenna in narration, no dialogue, no seventh shape (T050/T051 held). At the market's edge the foundling is a held shape, present but not registered as a new glimpse: the sixth sighting remains the sixth and is not counted a seventh in this chapter, no loaf, no slate, no sale, no half-beat, no dialogue, the green not joined to his sliver (T033/T034 held). Sella stands half a pace off with the basket in the moot-post's shade where no slate lay and gives no instruction to the basket; the reading does not answer the man carried out on Day 188, no figure, no collector and no slate knows what he cost, and the pale line stays on its own place, not laid across the told figure and the paid figure (T064/T061/T082). At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke before and river wind behind, going wide around the pan's gone ring, the bare dark trough, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line, with a look and a wide step and no number; the place the carriers crossed is gone around the same way and is not joined to any of them (T009/T013/T092/T098 carried). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen, sets the pot handle two inches beyond his hand, and does not touch the mark, because a reading and a dusk are not openings. In the small hours he lays out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel: six hearings with no seventh and none invented, the sixth out of a person filed beside and never among; three near-full answers advanced and unpaid; nine stoppings as objects and not a rule with no tenth before the seventh year is earned; three held changes on three places, the loft-sill scrape on a fourth and the carried man's pale line on a fifth, none stood up as a cause; the told bell beside the heard and the told figure beside the paid figure; the crust's empty place, the two shelf gaps, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch (T060/T086/T097/T100/T006 held). He wants the crust, the breast, the pot handle and a number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number counted, and gets none. One hundred and eighty-nine stands exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool.

scenes.title: The Account up the Road
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 190, Ember 11, Firstday, before first grey through the morning at the Vail kiln-house, the loaf shelf, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge and the Clay Yard. The month's first account has gone up the clay road in Berr's locked box and nothing in it can be undone; the printing still says one in twelve and nobody has challenged it. The boy is one hundred and ninety days old and six months and ten days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth is still missing under the floor with its payer unnamed for a hundred and ninety days (T088); the river's note and the boards' four nails, four and a knot keep the other two counts in their places (T061/T082). Hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner. Sella gives the instruction to wool, fire, pot, broom and running water and never the basket, says the house, keeps her half-pace and her jar-glance without a touch, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, feeds him barley gruel from the house's own dish with two fingers behind his ear, wipes the spoon on her sleeve and does not wipe his mouth (T058/T079). The district's arithmetic stays in arms, loaves, glances and weather: a woman who asks what the month will cost now the reading has gone up is sent to the pot and the weather with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, and carries the question away level, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077). Three or four unnamed men go low into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey and get no name; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third (T035/T031/T065/T095). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist opened, not bone-coloured slip; he keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, speaks to the wheel before anyone (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady), tells a pot You'll do, knows the full note three turns before it leaves the wheel and withholds the knowing from a man come up on the wrong wind, and when Sella's sentence goes low and unfinished his bent finger goes to the cold iron of the damper and waits until the words reach the pot, a remembered holding and not a new change (T061/T082, T062). The broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, entered by nobody; he's not Vail stays sealed and the promise to the slate-burners stays ungiven. At the kindling the small knife lies at the very edge of its sill, six years in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where no thumb has gone, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; Ash is worked into the creases of Tarn's knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifts it, and the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holds what light there is and gives it back. He takes the broom only after it has been instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while going on wanting the late because it puts off the paying, sweeps the collector's road without once turning along it, and no collector comes (T036/T076). The breath from Seed 16 stands unspent at the top of every reach with the small interval where a breath should have gone in and had not; the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes to his teeth and stands there with no figure and no name, drawn and not spent, and the nine stoppings stay nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the loan uncalled and the seventh year nearer its end than it has ever stood and not given (T036/T076, T061/T082). His stroke goes over the flagstones and the shallow bright patch without the half-check; the stone lies back in its unmarked clay pot in the Debt Loft, cold and unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving, and from below the boy files only a remembering and not a holding made again (T006). The charcoal waits unread beneath the loaf shelf and Sella's finger does not go beneath its front edge (T100).

scenes.title: What the Figure Does Not Know
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 190, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth, the bed and the clay road at the going of the light. The afternoon thins without ending, losing its edges the way water goes off a stone that has held the sun; hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner. Sella stands with her back to the basket at the loaf shelf and moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps, the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6, gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing without touching it, and keeps her finger from beneath the front edge, so the charcoal tally stays unread, uncounted, uncopied and the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left, an afternoon and a woman's back turned not the same as that night (T100). She told the fire it was the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, said The house will keep it where another woman would say I, stood a moment with the back of the pot in her hand counting under her breath toward no opening --- the small intake at the top, the hold, the letting go --- pushed coal-black hair back with the wrist that carries the little-door burn so the grey streak showed pale off the coals, set the pot rim out on the board with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand, and did not look toward the bed (T058/T079). At the kindling the knife is back where it can be checked, six counted and the seventh held; the ear-sentence comes to the threshold of the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, the breath drawn and not spent, no tenth stood up, the nine still nine, the Seed 16 breath still held, the loan uncalled (T036/T076). In the wheel-shed Jorra keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, gives the men in the back room no name, tells a pot You'll do, withholds its note, and holds his bent finger in the cold iron while Sella's unfinished sentence reaches the pot; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third, the two silences stay unjoined, and the promise of the foundling's name stays ungiven (T035/T031, T062, T065/T095). At the going of the light Sella carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her in long low bars and the river wind coming up behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough, the rack space and the empty place in the returning line, and around the place the carriers crossed on Day 188, with a look that asks for nothing and finds nothing, a wide step and no number and no explanation to the basket (T009/T013/T092/T098). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, base first and the weight settled the way a woman sets a vessel that must not rock, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without once looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed before it went away, and goes to her own bed. The widow's mark hangs on its cord where it has hung, touched once before the kiln on the first morning of Ember and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, afternoon or dusk since, because a dusk and a reading are not openings. The two rooms do not touch: hers holds a pot, a fire and a woman counting under her breath toward nothing entered, and his holds a crust two inches from an ear and an empty place beside it with no name. In the small hours he turns out the file: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, nine stoppings as objects and not a rule, three held changes on three places with the loft-sill scrape on a fourth and the carried man's pale line on a fifth, the told bell beside the heard and the told figure beside the paid figure. The month's figure went over the basket and did not know what the yard carried on its hands on Day 188; the cost stayed entered nowhere, no collector called, no figure given, no lesson made of the sweet wind or the pot that sang out early, and he made no cause across the pale line and any absence in the yard (T064/T077/T061/T082). One hundred and ninety stands exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool; he wants the crust, the breast, the pot handle and a number nobody will speak, and gets none.

scenes.title: The Tenth Day's Keeping
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 191, Ember 12, Secondday, before first grey into the morning at the Vail kiln-house, the Clay Yard, the yard well, the drying racks and the wheel-shed edge. The kiln month's second working week opens without a boundary drawn in the narration; the district keeps calling Tallow the firing month and Ember the kiln month and neither is corrected. The boy is one hundred and ninety-one days old and six months and eleven days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire answers four low pulls under the floor and misses its fifth, its payer unnamed for a hundred and ninety-one days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water and overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb, three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). The body humiliates him: the crust gone leathery two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, cold come to cheek, temple and the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back and stopped as if it had reached the end of its own order, the hand outside the wool going up an inch toward the river's note and coming down against the fold, the afterdrop waiting on the far side of a warming nobody in this house will perform. Sella gives the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, and leaves the widow's mark where it hangs, because a morning and a shelf are not openings and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1 (T058/T079). The yard's arithmetic stays in arms and loaves: a woman come up from the racks with slip dried pale in the creases of her wrists asks what the pots will want before the tend is out and is told to ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there; the question goes away level and leaves no entry (T077). The sweetish edge of lead glaze is spoken of as a direction on a wrong wind and answered with the pot and the weather, and the pot that sang itself out early on Day 188 stands swept around and is not made an omen; no second edge is paid so soon after the carrying-out and no High Kiln saying is made true as a lesson (T064/T077/T061/T082). The yard goes around the clean dark line where the Ash turned its corner for two years and the new finer grey called the thaw beside it, the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie, the pan's gone round place on the wall, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather, the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, and the place the carriers crossed on Day 188, each with a look that asks for nothing, a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092/T098 carried). Three or four men named by nobody are not on stage in these morning hours and the back room keeps its finger's width of open; the two tellings of a room shut in the war stay two with no third. Jorra, from the wheel-shed, keeps dust and clean forearms on one tray, speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot You'll do and keeps its full note from a man on the wrong wind; when Sella's voice goes low and unfinished at the hearth his bent finger goes to the cold iron of the damper and waits while the sentence reaches the pot, a remembered holding and not a change made again, not paired with the Day 166 beat beneath the shelf or the Day 171 flagstone half-check (T035/T031/T062). Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, says Six counted. The next I don't count to the kindling, six in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged sentence beside the knife, Ash in the knuckle creases, the pale clip-ring holding what light there is; the ear-sentence comes to his teeth and no further, no figure, no name, no tenth, the nine still nine, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled (T036/T076). The stone lies back in its pot in the loft, cold and unreconciled, and the boy keeps the remembering on its own place (T006).

scenes.title: Hand's Breadth toward the Water
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 191, Ember 12, Secondday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth, the bed and the clay road at the going of the light. The afternoon thins without ending; hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, the sour breath of the unswept corner. Sella stands at the loaf shelf with her back to the basket, moves her lips along a row with two unnamed gaps, gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, and keeps her finger from beneath the front edge, so the charcoal tally stays unread, uncounted, uncopied and the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left (T100). She tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands with the back of the pot in her hand counting under her breath toward no opening --- the small intake at the top, the hold, the letting go --- pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand, and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079). At the kindling the knife is back at the edge of its sill, six counted where the house can verify them and the seventh at the lip where no thumb has gone, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; the Seed 16 breath stands unspent at the top of every reach with the small interval where a breath should have gone in and had not; the ear-sentence comes to the threshold of the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, the breath drawn and not spent, the nine stoppings still nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the loan uncalled and the seventh year nearer its end than it has ever stood and not given; his stroke goes over the flagstones and the shallow bright patch without the half-check and the stones keep the place where it stopped and join it to nothing (T036/T076, T061/T082). The stone lies back in its unmarked clay pot in the loft, two years gone and cold, unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving; nothing from that room reaches the boy but the remembering he keeps on its own place, not a holding made again and not stood up with the three held changes or the loft-sill scrape into a rule (T006). At the going of the light Sella carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her in long low bars and the river wind coming up behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough, the rack space, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, with a look and a wide step and no number; under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen and unwiped, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, and has gone to her own bed, the two rooms not touching (T058/T079, T009/T013/T092/T098). In the small hours he turns out the file the way a man lays instruments on a towel before a case begins, each thing in its own hollow and nothing resting across anything else: six hearings of the full note beside and never among, five from four sources and the sixth, the small flat knock out of Dessa Silt as the men lifted, filed where a thing out of a person must go; no seventh came in a hundred and ninety-one days and none was invented to fill the empty place; three near-full answers advanced and not paid; the older intervals and the nine stoppings as objects with no payer named to any; the damper as one piece of iron with two bites joined to no kiln; three held changes on three separate places, the loft-sill scrape on a fourth, the two shut-room tellings side by side with no third, the told bell beside the heard, four, four and a gap, with nobody crossing himself, and the told figure beside the paid figure; the carried man's pale line on a fifth place of its own, exact, complete and worth nothing at two paces, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a near-full answer, not a stopping and not a fourth likeness stood up to call itself a cause; the sixth green a colour joined to no ear and the foundling a shape with no sale, both held and not advanced (T061/T082, T064, T050/T051, T033/T034). The shelf's two gaps, the fold's crust and its empty place, the pan's gone round ring and the field's empty place lie on trays that do not touch; no third gap came, no fourth likeness was made a cause and no finger of his drew the line (T060/T086/T097). He wants the crust two inches from his ear, the breast, the pot handle standing two inches beyond his hand and a number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number counted, and gets none, and has stopped expecting to be told, which is not the same as not wanting it. Through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, through the floor the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer without a name for a hundred and ninety-one days, and overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb --- three counts in three places, and none rises up and becomes the others. Ash lies thin along the skirting board in the colour of the clean dark line and the new finer grey called the thaw lies beside it, neither swept and neither with an instruction. One hundred and ninety-one stands exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, spoken by nobody under any roof; nothing has been joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, the nine stoppings are still nine with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath still held, the charcoal still waiting under the shelf, the mark touched once before the kiln and at no other hour, and the cost of the man carried out still entered nowhere. His hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water over water through the finger's-width door and comes down against the fold, and the count goes forward into Day 192, Ember 13.
